'''Sir Abel Guobadia''' [[Order of the Federal Republic|OFR]] (28 June 1932 – 4 February 2011) was an educator, administrator, diplomat and retired public servant.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.ilegrams.org/prominent.asp?idm=14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318220527/http://www.ilegrams.org/prominent.asp?idm=14|url-status=dead|archive-date=2011-03-18|title=Dr. Abel Ibude Guobadia|publisher=Ilesa Grammar School Alumni|access-date=2010-02-13}}</ref>

==Education==
Guobadia was born on 28 June 1932, in [[Benin City]], [[Nigeria]]. He attended C.M.S. Primary School in Benin City (1939–1945); [[Government College, Ibadan]] (1946–1951); [[University College Ibadan]] (1952–1957). In 1962, he won a scholarship for graduate studies in the United States of America and was awarded the Ph.D. in solid-state physics from the [[University of Pittsburgh]], Pennsylvania, US, in 1966.<ref name=bio/>

==Career==
Prior to enrolling for his Ph.D., Guobadia began his career as a physics teacher at Osogbo Grammar School (1957); Ilesha Grammar School (1958); Government College Ughelli (1958–1959); [[Edo College]], Benin City (1960); [[Government College, Ibadan|Government College Ibadan]] (1960–1961) and the [[University of Nigeria]], Nsukka (1961–1962). From 1966 - 1971, Guobadia was a Senior Lecturer and Head of Department of Physics at the [[University of Lagos]], Nigeria.<ref name=bio/>

Guobadia worked at Nigeria's [[National Universities Commission]] throughout most of the 1970s and early 1980s and rose to the position of Director of Academic Planning and subsequently, Executive Secretary of the Commission. In 1983, Guobadia helped the [[University of Benin (Nigeria)|University of Benin]], Benin City establish a Consultancy Services Unit and became the pioneer Director of the Unit.<ref name=bio/>

In January 1984, Guobadia was appointed Commissioner of Education for the defunct [[Bendel State]] of Nigeria under the military administration of Brigadier [[Jeremiah Useni]]. Later in 1986, the Colonel [[John Mark Inienger]] military administration appointed him the Bendel State Commissioner of Finance and Economic Planning.<ref name=guardian>{{cite news|title=The 2014 National Conference: Looking back, looking forward|url=https://guardian.ng/features/the-2014-national-conference-looking-back-looking-forward/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|date=2015-03-31|access-date=2020-05-24|newspaper=[[The Guardian (Nigeria)|The Guardian]]}}</ref>

In 1987, President [[Ibrahim Babangida]] appointed Guobadia as Nigeria's first resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the Republic of Korea.<ref>{{cite web|title=Embassy of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, South Korea|url=http://www.nigerianembassy.or.kr/embassy.htm|access-date=2010-02-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091015062242/http://www.nigerianembassy.or.kr/embassy.htm|archive-date=2009-10-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ex-INEC Boss, Guobadia Dies|url=https://www.pmnewsnigeria.com/2011/02/04/ex-inec-boss-guobadia-dies/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|date=2011-02-04|access-date=2020-05-25|newspaper=[[P.M. News]]}}</ref>

Upon retirement, Guobadia floated a private educational consulting firm, Advanced Educational Services Limited, that was responsible for developing academic programs for several universities in Nigeria. Guobadia and Professor [[T. M. Yesufu]] played an influential role in the establishment of the [[Igbinedion University]], Okada in Edo State, Nigeria.<ref>{{cite web|title=Igbinedion University Okada {{!}} history.php|url=https://www.iuokada.edu.ng/history.php|website=www.iuokada.edu.ng|access-date=2020-05-24|archive-date=2018-05-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180508193155/http://www.iuokada.edu.ng/history.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2000, the government of President [[Olusegun Obasanjo]] appointed Guobadia Nigeria's Chief Electoral Officer. Guobadia was confirmed as the Chairman of Nigeria's [[Independent National Electoral Commission (Nigeria)|Independent National Electoral Commission]] by the Nigerian Senate in May 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ifes.org/publication/d5cdd8094465e31baf096f4eba5d457c/Et9_1.pdf|title=Abel Guobadia Takes Helm in Nigeria|work=Elections Today|access-date=2010-02-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081128123048/http://www.ifes.org/publication/d5cdd8094465e31baf096f4eba5d457c/Et9_1.pdf|archive-date=2008-11-28}}</ref>

Guobada retired from this position in May 2005<ref name=van>{{cite news|date=2011-02-04|title=Abel Guobadia, ex-INEC chairman dies at 78|url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2011/02/abel-guobadia-ex-inec-chairman-dies-at-78/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2022-03-18|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref> becoming the first Chairman of the Electoral Commission since Nigeria's independence in 1960, to complete his tenure.

Guobadia has served as chairman and/or member of many boards, including that of the [[New Nigeria Bank]], [[West African Examinations Council]] and the [[Standards Organisation of Nigeria|Standards Organization of Nigeria]]. He has served in several capacities on Governing Councils of several universities in Nigeria. Guobadia was former Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council of the [[Edo State University]], [[Ekpoma]]. Guobadia was the President of the [[Science Teachers Association of Nigeria]] (STAN) from 1971 to 1976 and remains an honorary life fellow of STAN. He is a Special Member of the Senate of the [[University of Benin (Nigeria)|University of Benin]], Benin City.<ref name=guardian/>

In seeking to advance the development of his cosmopolitan Edo community in mid-western Nigeria, Guobadia worked as the secretary of the Benin Forum and chairman of the Edo Forum respectively from 1992 to 2000.

Guobadia served as chairman of the board of trustees of a prominent non-governmental organisation, Women's Health and Action Research Centre (WHARC) located in Benin City, Nigeria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wharc-online.org/about-wharc/board-trustees/dr-abel-guobadia-phd|title=Dr. Abel Guobadia, PhD|publisher=Women's Health and Action Research Centre|access-date=2010-02-13}} {{Dead link|date=June 2017|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> Guobadia died on 4 February 2011, at the age of 78.<ref name=van/>
